title: Feature Importance Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Rank five housing features by standardized coefficient, permutation importance, and drop-column importance, and find out why the three rankings disagree when features are correlated.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to compare standardized coefficients, permutation importance, and drop-column importance for one model, identify the features on which the methods disagree, and explain the disagreement in terms of correlation between features.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison of three rankings with a correlation switch and a per-feature inspection panel
keyQuestions: Which feature is the most important? Does your answer depend on the method?
Why does removing square_feet cost the model less than shuffling it?
Why do the dashed and red lines for bedrooms have such different slopes when the features are correlated?
commonMisconceptions: The feature with the largest raw coefficient is the most important (raw coefficients depend on the units, so features must be standardized before their coefficients are compared).
Feature importance is a single fixed property of a feature (it depends on the method, on the other features in the model, and on the sample).
A feature with a small drop-column importance is useless (it may carry information that a correlated feature can also supply).
Permutation importance gives the same numbers every time (each run uses different random shuffles, so it varies by about its error bar).
assessmentOpportunities: Students explain why a feature can have a large permutation importance and a small drop-column importance in the same model, and state what kind of data makes all three methods agree.
